svg.title: Triple Balance: a compressed decision diagram
svg.desc: Pay once for zero to three technologies, then follow six policy rounds, three random-event slots, and up to three technology choices. Events follow policy rounds 1, 3 and 4; technology slots follow rounds 2, 5 and 6. Each policy has three options; each event slot has seven routes. Technology slots are skipped automatically unless paid for. Dashed red branches end at Game Over when happiness or money reaches zero. Lines rejoin to save space, but different routes keep their own resources. There are 3,597,500 successful playthroughs and 456,680 early endings, totalling 4,054,180.
svg.text: If n = 0, 1, 2, or 3, then thre are 1, 3, 9, or 27 branches, respectively.
One game, millions of possible paths
A compressed decision diagram: every route keeps its own choices and resources.
1. Pay for research before the first policy round
No event, or an event with 2 responses.
If n ≥ 1: choose 1 of 3. Otherwise: skip.
No event, or an event with 2 responses.
No event, or an event with 2 responses.
If n ≥ 2: choose 1 of 3. Otherwise: skip.
If n = 3: choose 1 of 3. Otherwise: skip.
Each option continues with its own resources.
Each slot has its own events. You choose the response.
Response 1 or 2 for each event; no response for “no event”.
These seven routes are not equally likely.
Technology slots depend on the initial payment
Dashed red branches: stop at Game Over
After a policy or event response, stop if:
• happiness is zero or below, or
• the budget is zero or below.
Do not count any decisions after that point.
Full plans if we ignore Game Over: 3⁶ × 7³ × (1 + 3 + 9 + 27) = 10,001,880
Count each visible path once. Exclude restarts and explanation/credits detours. Counts are not probabilities.
